sample.name: Rinconada Park
facts: Established in 1922 as Waterworks and renamed Rinconada two years later.
Home to the city's municipal swimming pool.
Address: 777 Embarcadero Rd, Palo Alto

sample.name: Bedwell Bayfront Park
facts: A 160-acre nature park built on a capped landfill, with construction from 1982 to 1995.
A 2.3-mile perimeter trail is part of the San Francisco Bay Trail.
Surrounded on three sides by the Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge.

sample.name: Sunnyvale Baylands Park
facts: Has over 70 acres of developed parkland plus a 105-acre seasonal wetlands preserve.
Santa Clara County owns the property and the City of Sunnyvale manages the park.
The park has an outdoor turf amphitheater and access to the San Francisco Bay Trail.

sample.name: Cuesta Park
facts: The park has a bocce court, off-leash dog area, playground and tennis court.
A free outdoor Fitness Court with 10 pieces of equipment was added with a grant from El Camino Health.
Address: 615 Cuesta Dr, Mountain View

sample.name: Peers Park
facts: Has redwoods grown from seeds that orbited aboard Space Shuttle Challenger in 1985.
Named for Alexander Peers, first president of Mayfield's bank.
Address: 1899 Park Blvd, Palo Alto

sample.name: McClellan Ranch Preserve
facts: An 18-acre preserve on a former horse ranch from the 1930s and 40s.
Home to the Environmental Education Center and a recreated Baer Blacksmith Shop.
Address: 22221 McClellan Road, Cupertino

sample.name: Eleanor Pardee Park
facts: A 9.6-acre neighborhood park with community gardens.
Named for Eleanor Pardee; her mother deeded the property to the city in 1920.
Address: 851 Center Dr, Palo Alto

sample.name: Parque de los Pobladores
facts: A 0.2 acre park in SoFA at Market Street and South 1st Street.
Holds a 1997 monument to the founding of the Pueblo de San Jose de Guadalupe by the Anza Expedition settlers.
Redeveloped in 2012 under the city's Pavement to Plaza program.

sample.name: Elizabeth F. Gamble Garden
facts: Elizabeth Gamble left her house and garden to the city on her death in 1981.
Became a public garden in 1985, supported by a nonprofit horticultural foundation.
Elizabeth Gamble was the granddaughter of Procter & Gamble co-founder James Gamble.

sample.name: Corn Palace Park
facts: The 2-acre park sits on former Francia family farmland that ran the Corn Palace farmstand from 1965 to 2015.
The park opened on June 27, 2025.
Run by City of Sunnyvale

sample.name: Redwood Grove Nature Preserve
facts: The six-acre preserve was purchased in 1974.
The Halsey House inside the preserve was built in 1923 and is a local Historic Landmark.
Established in 1974

sample.name: Byxbee Park
facts: Opened in 1991 with earthworks by Peter Richards and Michael Oppenheimer.
Designated as an art park within the Baylands Preserve.
Run by City of Palo Alto

sample.name: Memorial Park
facts: The 22-acre park has an amphitheater, a gazebo and the Cupertino Veterans Memorial.
The park is next to the Cupertino Senior Center, Quinlan Community Center and Cupertino Sports Center.
Address: 21121 Stevens Creek Blvd, Cupertino

sample.name: Bol Park
facts: A 13.8-acre park in Barron Park bordered by Matadero Creek.
Named for Stanford physicist Cornelis Bol, who bought the donkey pasture in the 1930s.
Opened to the public in April 1974.

sample.name: Heritage Park
facts: Opened on March 12, 2006 on the former Palo Alto Medical Foundation site.
A sentinel redwood anchors the 2.01-acre park.
Address: 300 Homer Ave, Palo Alto

sample.name: Rengstorff Park
facts: Opened as Mountain View Recreation Center Park and was renamed Rengstorff Park in 1970.
Rengstorff Avenue was called Pastoria Avenue until 1929, after the Castro family's Rancho Pastoria de las Borregas.
Address: 201 S Rengstorff Ave, Mountain View
